## Body

# Security review: PR #263, round 1

Head: `2b0ce696554bd03a023193a584f916a904a160e9`
Result: **pass-with-notes**. No introduced exploitable vulnerability identified within C33's user-account trust boundary.

## Evidence

- Claims supply a candidate host, not an ancestor list. The daemon constructs private `NativeHandoff` proof after following observed process parents, verifying the Copilot host and reaching the observed pane process. `claim.parent` is the governing-seat relationship, not process ancestry (`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:104-114,613-663,720-828`; kernel parent reads: `crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:338-355`). Non-native and reclaim registration modes receive no native carry proof (`registration.rs:167-201,847-852`; `http/identity.rs:1098-1111`).
- Carry requires a stored proxied stamp and membership of its exact PID/start identity in the verified ancestor list. `ProcIdentity` equality includes both fields (`crates/core/src/model.rs:336-343`; `registration.rs:1191-1225`). The chain is observed and rechecked; missing/dead or changed identities cannot establish carry. A live matching ancestor is required.
- Registration records the replacement process identity, allowing further verified descendants to carry. Opt-outs are preserved; non-descendants lose the stale stamp; revive keeps its newly gated stamp (`registration.rs:1179-1258`; `crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1548-1561`). The fixed carried reason explicitly says the route was not re-read (`crates/core/src/model.rs:603-634`).
- The nine-file delta adds no production environment/token reads, logging, secret persistence or process launches. The extension and `crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs` are unchanged. Changed docs, public PR text and new commit messages contain no newly introduced private owner/repository identities or user-specific home paths.

## Guard proof: assertions read, not executed

- `a_reused_pid_carries_no_route` varies start while retaining PID and expects no stamp: PID-only matching would fail it (`registration.rs:3479-3486`).
- `a_process_outside_the_stamped_lineage_reads_plain` shares the pane but not the stamped ancestry and expects no stamp: removing descendant membership or using pane identity would fail it (`registration.rs:3491-3497`).
- Restart coverage asserts proxied state, exact reason, no fix and acceptance of an already-carried stamp (`registration.rs:3461-3473`). Opt-out and fresh revive assertions are at `3501-3513,3518-3531`. The changing-start-during-observation regression requires refusal and an empty registry (`5152-5180`).
- The transitive fixture proves carried-stamp eligibility, not two consecutive real process replacements.

## Non-blocking note and known limits

`docs/difficulties.md:175` and the PR text propose a filtered manual `ps -Eww` diagnostic. This is an operator environment-reading command, not the daemon's implementation. Its pipeline filters final stdout, not the environment read itself, and should not be described as a secret-safe capture/redaction mechanism. No diagnostic or live environment inspection was performed; no actual token exposure was established. Clarifying that assurance is recommended, not a blocking security finding.

The daemon verifies a claimed live host tuple; it does not authenticate that the HTTP caller executes inside that host. This is the existing C33 boundary. Carry is routing lineage evidence, not live environment/account/model/proxy-readiness attestation. Pre-fix restarts whose stamp was erased remain plain until revived, as documented.

## Validation and proof limits

`just pr-freeze 263` passed: remote and GitHub heads agree, CLEAN, ready, no migration, latest CI `check (22)`, `check (24)`, `rust-lint`, `rust-test` and `delivers` passed. The detached worktree is clean. The spawn-sites diff is empty. Added work is in-process at new-process registration; no new recurring loop, poll, timer or launch was identified.

Source/caller/test inspection was performed by the security-review agent. The role holder independently verified finality, CI status, changed-file boundaries, public PR metadata and new commit messages. No local builds, test or mutation runs, dependency installs, restarts or `harness checks` were performed under the reviewer contract. Live post-merge restart proof remains with the owning PM.

Harness feedback: retain the distinction between an output-filtered operator diagnostic and a secret-safe capture; record this in security role memory rather than adding production environment inspection.
